bd-pyrrhura-molinae.title: Green-Cheeked Conure
bd-pyrrhura-molinae.summary: One of the smallest and quietest conures and a favorite for people ready to move up from a small bird. Green cheeks are playful little clowns, affectionate and not known to be nippy, and come in color mutations such as pineapple, cinnamon, turquoise and yellow-sided.
rows: 25–30 years with proper care (the average is much shorter due to poor diet or neglect)
A spacious cage with plenty of toys to rotate; lots of daily time out of the cage
A balanced manufactured (pellet-based) diet with fresh vegetables, fruit and healthy table foods; seeds alone are not enough. Never chocolate, caffeine or avocado
Very affectionate and needs a lot of daily attention; can be kept in pairs and stay tame with daily handling
Relatively quiet for a conure but will make some noise; some learn a few words
Generally good-natured and small enough for older children with supervision; any bird can bite
Forests and woodland of Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina and Paraguay
warn: Prone to feather picking if bored; give lots of toys, foraging and chew items.

bd-aratinga-jandaya.title: Jenday Conure
bd-aratinga-jandaya.summary: A bright orange, yellow and green conure from northeastern Brazil and a close relative of the extinct Carolina parakeet. Jendays are trusting, playful and smart enough to learn tricks, but like all Aratinga conures they're fairly loud.
rows: Up to about 30 years in captivity
At least 36 × 24 × 24 in (L × W × H); a cockatiel-size cage is too small
A balanced manufactured (pellet-based) diet with fresh vegetables, fruit and healthy table foods; seeds alone are not enough. Never chocolate, caffeine or avocado
Needs a lot of daily time out of the cage; can be paired with another Jenday (or a sun or similar conure for company only)
Moderately loud; can learn to talk a little
Trusting; hand-fed Jendays are not known to become nippy
Wooded habitats and palm groves of northeastern Brazil
notes: Young birds are mostly green with a mottled yellow head; the full color comes with maturity.

bd-aratinga-solstitialis.title: Sun Conure
bd-aratinga-solstitialis.summary: A brilliantly orange-and-yellow conure from northeastern South America. Sun conures are playful, adventurous and very attached to their people, but they're vocal birds that will do their share of screaming.
rows: About 15–25 years with good care (up to 30 reported)
A large cage plus plenty of play time outside it; birds kept in small cages tend to become overweight
A balanced manufactured (pellet-based) diet with fresh vegetables, fruit and healthy table foods; seeds alone are not enough. Never chocolate, caffeine or avocado
Loves attention and does not like being left alone; can be paired with another Aratinga conure for company
Loud: a vocal species that will scream at times
notes: Young birds take about two years to reach full color.

bd-thectocercus-acuticaudatus.title: Blue-Crowned Conure
bd-thectocercus-acuticaudatus.summary: A green conure with a blue head and a long, pointed tail, known as one of the better talkers among conures. It's social and needs lots of interaction, and it can be loud and persistent.
rows: About 14.5–16 in (37–40 cm) including the long tail; 140–190 g
A balanced manufactured (pellet-based) diet with fresh vegetables, fruit and healthy table foods; seeds alone are not enough. Never chocolate, caffeine or avocado
Not content to be left alone in a cage; needs lots of interaction
Loud and vocally persistent; one of the more talkative conures
South America, from Colombia to Argentina

bd-aratinga-nenday.title: Nanday Conure
bd-aratinga-nenday.summary: A green conure with a black hood, blue-washed throat and red thighs, from the lowlands of Paraguay, Bolivia, Brazil and Argentina. Nandays are social and long-lived but famously loud, with screeching calls.
rows: Large cage or aviary with plenty of flying room (about 6.5–10 ft long is recommended for aviaries)
Varied diet: fruit (about 30%), vegetables and leafy greens, spray millet and a small seed mix
Very sociable; needs daily interaction, baths, ladders, swings, puzzle and foraging toys and safe chews
Loud: screeching flight calls and shrill chatter
Paraguay, southeastern Bolivia, southwestern Brazil and northern Argentina (feral flocks in Florida and California)

bd-psittacara-mitratus.title: Mitred Conure
bd-psittacara-mitratus.summary: A large green conure from the Andean woodlands of Peru, Bolivia and Argentina. Mitreds are active, avid bathers and strong chewers with loud, harsh calls.
rows: Large cage or aviary (about 6.5 ft long recommended for aviaries)
Varied diet: fruit (about 30%), vegetables and leafy greens, spray millet and a small seed mix
Needs daily interaction; loves bathing (misters or a shallow bowl) and chewing (safe branches, wood and leather toys)
Andean woodland and scrub of Peru, Bolivia and Argentina

bd-aratinga-weddellii.title: Dusky-Headed Conure
bd-aratinga-weddellii.summary: A small green conure with a soft grey-brown head and white eye-ring, from forests of the western Amazon. Flocks call with continuous shrieks.
rows: Large cage or aviary (about 6.5 ft long recommended for aviaries)
Varied diet: fruit (about 30%), vegetables and leafy greens, spray millet and a small seed mix
Needs daily interaction, safe chew toys and a bowl for bathing
Calls are shrieks of four or five notes, especially in groups
Western Amazon basin: Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil and Bolivia

bd-psittacara-erythrogenys.title: Cherry-Headed (Red-Masked) Conure
bd-psittacara-erythrogenys.summary: A bright green conure with a mostly red head, from Ecuador and Peru, often called the best talker of the conures. It's a vigorous chewer with raspy, screechy calls.
rows: About 13 in (33 cm), half of it tail; about 165–200 g
Up to about 25 years (10–15 on average)
Large, metal cage or aviary (about 6.5–10 ft long recommended for aviaries)
Varied diet: fruit (about 30%), vegetables and leafy greens, spray millet and a small seed mix
Needs daily interaction and lots of safe things to chew (branches, wood blocks, leather toys) plus puzzle and foraging toys
Loud: raspy, screechy calls; known as a good talker

bd-eupsittula-pertinax.title: Brown-Throated Conure
bd-eupsittula-pertinax.summary: A small green conure with a brown throat, from Panama, Costa Rica, northern South America and nearby Caribbean islands. It's an avid chewer and very noisy, calling constantly in flight.
rows: Large cage or aviary (about 6.5 ft long recommended for aviaries)
Varied diet: fruit (about 30%), vegetables and leafy greens, spray millet and a small seed mix
Enjoys interaction and bathing; needs plenty of safe woods, branches and puzzle or foraging toys
Costa Rica, Panama, northern South America and islands off the Caribbean coast
